title: Battery Runtime Estimator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A calculator that estimates robot runtime as usable battery capacity divided by total current. Students choose a 4 x AA alkaline or 2S LiPo pack, set motor duty and battery health, switch the OLED and NeoPixels on or off, and watch a battery gauge drain.

educational.topic: Battery capacity, current draw, and runtime
learningObjectives: Calculate battery runtime as usable capacity (mAh) divided by total current (mA).
Add the robot's individual loads to find the total current.
Apply the alkaline high-current derating and the LiPo 80 percent limit to find usable capacity.
Explain how motor duty changes the runtime.
standards: CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.6.RP.A.3: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Calculator with a live worked formula so students can check hand calculations
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Students choose a battery, adjust motor duty and battery health sliders, toggle loads, and read the runtime and the formula strip; Run drains the gauge at 1 simulated hour per second.
keyQuestions: Which load uses the most current?
Why does a LiPo pack only use 80 percent of its rated capacity?
What happens to the runtime when you halve the motor duty?
Which pack lasts longer at 100 percent motor duty, and why?
commonMisconceptions: A higher-voltage pack always runs longer.
mAh and mA measure the same thing.
All of a battery's rated capacity can be used at any current.
The display and LEDs use as much current as the motors.
assessmentOpportunities: Verify the default runtime by hand calculation.
Challenge: compare the AA pack and the 1000 mAh LiPo at 100 percent duty.
Exit ticket: estimate runtime for a 250 mA load on a 2000 mAh LiPo.
